source_document.body:
Robert Friedland in 2014 at the site of the initial Kamoa discovery in DRC. ( Image: Govind Friedland via CEO.ca )
Posted By: Cecilia Jamasmie November 19, 2026
Ivanhoe Electric (NYSE American: IE; TSX: IE), backed by mining billionaire Robert Friedland, has discovered high-grade copper-gold-silver mineralization at its Gleeson project in southeastern Arizona, making it the company’s top exploration priority.
The company reporte d Thursday that drilling identified two mineralized zones, including 123.6 metres grading 0.91% copper, 0.44 gram of gold per tonne and 5.27 grams of silver per tonne from a depth of 601.7 metres. The interval included 71.03 metres grading 1.38% copper, 0.52 gram of gold and 6.73 grams of silver.
“These initial drill results are some of the best copper-gold-silver intercepts drilled in the Western United States in the last 10 years,” Executive Chairman Friedland and President and CEO Taylor Melvin said in a joint statement.
The discovery, 45 km north of Arizona’s historic Bisbee mining district, could provide another growth opportunity alongside Ivanhoe Electric’s Santa Cruz copper project near Casa Grande, where it plans to produce refined copper domestically.
Copper drop
Shares in Ivanhoe Electric fell 2.6% to C$8.33 apiece by Thursday afternoon, valuing the company at about C$1.33 billion. Wider markets declined as investors appeared to be selling on the rally created by the widely anticipated Anthropic initial public offering.
The drill results come as copper prices plunged about 6% this week to $12,471 per tonne on the London Metal Exchange, their lowest since April. Investors have been unwinding bets on artificial intelligence-driven demand and potential US tariffs on refined copper, with the sell-off accelerating after billionaire investor Stan Druckenmiller turned bearish .
The decline contrasts with tight physical supplies in China, where the Yangshan copper import premium reached a record $360 per tonne, up from less than $100 in September. Shanghai Futures Exchange inventories fell 18% over the week to 27,600 tonnes, their lowest since December 2023, highlighting the divide between investor sentiment and physical market conditions.
Two zones
Ivanhoe Electric spent $4.7 million (C$6.7 million) on exploration and evaluation at Gleeson in the quarter to Sept. 30, up from $219,000 a year earlier, the company said in a filing. Two rigs are working towards 16,000 metres by year-end, including drilling completed since November 2025.
Drilling at Gleeson has outlined an upper copper-gold-silver-bearing breccia zone spanning approximately 500 by 500 metres, beginning around 600 metres below surface. The mineralization thickens southwestward and remains open in several directions.
A second hole, CGD26-TR-008, returned 381.66 metres grading 0.34% copper, 0.29 gram of gold and 1.07 grams of silver per tonne from 587.85 metres. It included 16.2 metres grading 1.04% copper and a separate 41.51-metre interval grading 1.23 grams of gold.
Deeper drilling, below 1,000 metres, identified intrusive-hosted, skarn and carbonate-replacement mineralization containing copper, gold, silver and zinc. The system extends roughly 800 metres north to south and 600 metres east to west, with further potential to the west.
“The initial drill holes at Gleeson are the most impressive I have seen in my 20-year career at an early-stage exploration project,” Senior Vice-President of Exploration Alex Neufeld said.
Bisbee district
Neufeld compared Gleeson’s geology with the nearby Bisbee district, which produced more than 200 million tonnes of ore over 133 years.
Ivanhoe Electric controls approximately 20,000 acres of mineral rights and more than 2,000 acres of private surface rights at Gleeson, although drilling has tested only a small portion of the property.
Since November 2025, the company has completed 11 drill holes, receiving full assays for seven and partial results for two. Two rigs are operating, with 16,000 metres of drilling targeted by year-end. Additional holes have encountered visible sulphide mineralization, including deeper carbonate-replacement zones beginning around 1,250 metres below surface.
Gleeson remains an early-stage discovery without a defined mineral resource or demonstrated economic viability. Further drilling must establish the continuity, scale and true widths of the mineralized zones.
American copper
The discovery strengthens Ivanhoe Electric’s Arizona portfolio as it advances Santa Cruz, a proposed high-grade underground mine on private land near Casa Grande.
Santa Cruz is designed to produce refined copper cathode through hydrometallurgical processing, including solvent extraction and electrowinning, eliminating the need for conventional smelting or overseas concentrate refining.
The approach could help supply US manufacturers directly while reducing exposure to international processing bottlenecks and certain trade risks, aligning with Washington’s efforts to secure domestic copper supplies for electricity networks, defence and manufacturing.
Friedland, whose ventures have included some of the world’s largest copper discoveries, sees Gleeson as a potential new mineral district in the American Southwest.
